Absentee & Mail Ballots

Office
Town Clerk — Town Hall, Room 102
Phone
(774) 555-0102
Email
clerk@millbrook-ma.gov
Fee
None

Any registered Millbrook voter may request a ballot by mail for any election. Ballots may be returned by mail, dropped at a secure ballot box, or returned in person to the Town Clerk’s office before polls close.

How to request

  1. Complete a Ballot Application (paper or online).
  2. Submit no later than five business days before Election Day.
  3. You will receive your ballot within 2–3 business days of approval.

Required information

  • Voter’s legal name and Millbrook residence address
  • Mailing address (if different)
  • Signature matching your voter registration
Ballot Application Form Request online Drop-box locations

Assessor — Property Search & Abatements

Office
Assessor — Town Hall, Room 105
Phone
(774) 555-0104
Hours
Mon–Thu 8:30–4:30, Fri 8:30–1:00
Fee
Property cards: free online; $1/page at counter

Look up the assessed value, ownership history, lot size, and tax record of any property in Millbrook. Property owners who believe their assessment is incorrect may file an abatement within the statutory window following the issuance of the third-quarter tax bill.

How to file an abatement

  1. Obtain the State Tax Form 128 (Application for Abatement).
  2. Submit to the Assessor’s office by February 1 following the bill date.
  3. The Board of Assessors will respond within three months.

Required documents

  • Completed Form 128
  • Recent comparable sales (if available)
  • Photographs documenting conditions affecting value
Search property records Form 128 — Abatement FY26 Assessor’s Annual Report

Services beginning with B

Building Permits

Office
Building & Planning — Town Hall, Room 207
Inspector
James P. Carrigan, CBO
Phone
(774) 555-0106
Fees
From $75 (minor) to $0.40 per square foot of new construction

A building permit is required for most structural alterations, additions, new construction, demolitions, roof replacement, decks, sheds over 200 sq. ft., swimming pools, and replacement windows. Permits ensure work meets the Massachusetts State Building Code and town zoning bylaws.

How to apply

  1. Pre-apply online or pick up an application at Room 207.
  2. Submit two sets of construction drawings, a site plan, and a contractor’s license copy.
  3. The Building Inspector reviews within 10 business days.
  4. Once issued, post the permit visibly at the work site.
  5. Schedule required inspections (foundation, framing, insulation, final).

Required documents

  • Completed application signed by the property owner
  • Two sets of stamped construction drawings (if applicable)
  • Site plan showing all setbacks
  • Workers’ compensation affidavit
  • HIC and CSL license copies for contractors

From $75 Minor work (e.g., re-roof, shed). New construction $0.40/sq. ft. plus $75 base.

Apply online Fee schedule (FY27) Application packet Inspection requests

Bulk-Item Pickup

Office
Department of Public Works
Phone
(774) 555-0105
Schedule
Tuesdays, by appointment
Fee
$25 per item (furniture, appliances)

The DPW collects large household items that cannot fit in a standard curbside barrel. Pickup is available Tuesdays between 7:00 a.m. and 1:00 p.m. by appointment, scheduled at least one week in advance. Items must be at the curb by 6:30 a.m.

Accepted items

  • Mattresses and box springs (wrapped in plastic)
  • Couches, chairs, tables, dressers
  • Refrigerators and freezers (must be CFC-tagged)
  • Stoves, dishwashers, washing machines, dryers
  • Televisions and computer monitors

Not accepted

  • Construction debris, tires, paint, automotive fluids
  • Items containing hazardous waste (must use household haz-waste days)
Schedule pickup Accepted items list Household haz-waste calendar

Burning Permits (Brush)

Office
Fire Department — 4 Cobbett Square
Phone
(774) 555-0111
Season
January 15 – May 1 only
Fee
$10 annual permit

Open burning of brush, cane, driftwood, and forestry debris is permitted in Millbrook from January 15 through May 1 each year, in accordance with state law. Burning is only allowed between 10:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. on days when conditions are deemed safe by the Fire Department.

How to obtain

  1. Purchase the annual permit at the Fire Department or online.
  2. Activate the permit by calling the burn line each morning you wish to burn.
  3. Confirm conditions are safe before lighting.

Restrictions

  • Materials must be brush, not construction debris or trash.
  • Burn pile must be at least 75 ft. from any structure.
  • An adult must attend the fire at all times with water on hand.
Daily burn line: (774) 555-0190 State burning regulations

Phone
(774) 555-0120

Single plot $700 (resident), $1,400 (non-resident)

The town maintains four cemeteries: Old Burying Ground (1739, historic only), Pine Hill Cemetery, Cobbett River Cemetery, and Veterans Memorial Cemetery. Plot sales and burial scheduling are handled by the Cemetery Commission. Historical records dating to 1739 are available for genealogical research.

To purchase a plot

  1. Contact the Commission to confirm availability in your preferred section.
  2. Schedule an in-person visit to select a location.
  3. Sign the deed of right and pay the perpetual care fee.

Required documents

  • Photo identification

Dog Licenses

Office
Town Clerk — Town Hall, Room 102
Phone
(774) 555-0102
Renewal due
April 30 annually
Late fee
$25 after May 31

All dogs aged six months or older that reside in Millbrook must be licensed annually. Licenses run April 1 through March 31 and may be renewed in person, by mail, or online. Proof of current rabies vaccination is required.

How to apply or renew

  1. Bring or upload a copy of your dog’s current rabies certificate.
  2. Bring proof of spay/neuter for the discounted rate.
  3. Pay the applicable fee.
  4. You will receive a metal tag for your dog’s collar.

$20 spayed/neutered $35 unaltered $5 service dog

Kennel licenses (4+ dogs) start at $75/year. Replacement tag: $5.

Excise Tax (Motor Vehicle)

Office
Tax Collector — Town Hall, Room 103
Phone
(774) 555-0103
Rate
$25.00 per $1,000 of valuation (state-set)
Due
30 days from bill date

Massachusetts levies an annual excise tax on all motor vehicles registered to a Millbrook address. The tax is billed once per year, typically in February or March, based on the vehicle’s manufacturer’s list price and age. Failure to pay can result in license and registration suspension.

How to pay

  1. Pay online with bill number and license plate.
  2. Mail check or money order to: Town of Millbrook, P.O. Box 47, Millbrook, MA 02XXX.
  3. Pay in person at the Tax Collector window or use the drop box outside Town Hall.

Abatement

If you sold, traded, or moved the vehicle out of Massachusetts during the tax year, you may apply for an abatement. Required documentation includes a plate-return receipt from the RMV and a bill of sale or new state registration.

Pay excise tax Excise abatement application

Facility & Field Reservations

Office
Recreation & Parks — Memorial Hall, lower level
Phone
(774) 555-0130
Lead time
At least 14 days in advance
Fees
Varies by facility (see fee schedule)

Residents, town committees, and non-profit organizations may reserve town-owned spaces for meetings, parties, ceremonies, and recreational events. Available spaces include the Memorial Hall main room, Common Park Bandstand, Cobbett Park pavilions, athletic fields, and Senior Center community room.

How to reserve

  1. Check facility availability on the online calendar.
  2. Submit a Facility Use Application at least 14 days before your event.
  3. Provide a certificate of liability insurance ($1M minimum).
  4. Pay rental and refundable cleaning deposit upon approval.

Sample fees (per use)

  • Memorial Hall main room: $150 resident / $300 non-resident
  • Common Park Bandstand: $75 resident / $200 non-resident
  • Athletic field (per game): $40 resident / $100 non-resident
  • Senior Center community room: $50 resident / $150 non-resident

Non-profit organizations qualify for resident pricing with 501(c)(3) documentation. Town committees and youth sports leagues do not pay rental fees.

Check availability Facility Use Application Full fee schedule

Flu & Vaccination Clinics

Office
Health Department — Town Hall, Room 109
Phone
(774) 555-0107
Season
October – December annually
Cost
Free with insurance; $25 self-pay

The Health Department offers free seasonal flu vaccinations at multiple community locations each fall. Clinics are open to all Millbrook residents aged six months and older. High-dose vaccines are available for residents 65 and older.

What to bring

  • Photo identification
  • Insurance card (we bill most major insurers; nothing owed)
  • Completed consent form (available at clinic or download)

The Department also coordinates COVID-19 boosters, pneumonia vaccinations for at-risk adults, and travel-related vaccinations by appointment.

Phone

December 31 annually

All establishments serving or selling food in Millbrook must hold a current food establishment permit issued by the Board of Health. Permits are granted following plan review, on-site inspection, and verification of certified food protection manager presence.

Categories & fees

  • Retail food establishment (under 50 seats): $200
  • Full-service restaurant (50+ seats): $450

Library Card & Borrowing

Office
Public Library — 22 Cobbett Square
Phone
(774) 555-0140
Hours
Mon–Thu 9–8, Fri–Sat 9–5, Sun 1–5
Fee
Free for residents

The Millbrook Public Library is part of the SAILS Library Network and offers borrowing privileges across 70 member libraries. Resident library cards are free; non-residents may obtain a card for $35 per year. The library lends books, audiobooks, ebooks, DVDs, museum passes, hot spots, and tools.

To get a card

  2. Present photo ID and proof of Millbrook residency (utility bill, lease, tax bill).

Marriage Licenses

Office
Town Clerk — Town Hall, Room 102
Phone
(774) 555-0102
Waiting period
3 calendar days (state-required)
Fee
$50 (cash, check, or money order)

Couples may apply for a Massachusetts marriage license in any city or town in the Commonwealth. Both parties must appear in person to complete the Notice of Intention. The license is valid for 60 days from the third day after application and may be used anywhere in Massachusetts.

How to apply

  1. Both parties appear in person at the Town Clerk’s office.
  2. Complete the Notice of Intention form together.
  3. Present photo identification (driver’s license, passport).
  4. Wait the mandatory three-day period.
  5. Return to pick up the license, valid for 60 days.

Required documents

  • Government-issued photo ID for each party
  • Date and place of birth for each party
  • Parents’ full names (including maiden names)
  • Divorce decree or death certificate if previously married
Intention of Marriage form Justice of the Peace list

Open Meeting Law Complaints

Office
Town Clerk — Town Hall, Room 102
Phone
(774) 555-0102
Statute
M.G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18–25
Fee
None

Massachusetts Open Meeting Law guarantees the public’s right to observe deliberations of public bodies. Any person may file a complaint alleging a violation. Complaints must be filed within 30 days of the alleged violation with the public body and the Attorney General’s Division of Open Government.

How to file

  1. Complete the Open Meeting Law Complaint Form.
  2. File the original with the public body (chair or clerk).
  3. File a copy with the AG’s Division of Open Government.
  4. The public body has 14 business days to respond.
Complaint form OML guide for the public

Polling Places & Election Day

Office
Town Clerk — Town Hall, Room 102
Phone
(774) 555-0102
Polls open
7:00 a.m. – 8:00 p.m.
Precincts
Four (4) in Millbrook

Millbrook is divided into four voting precincts. Your precinct is determined by your residential address and is printed on your voter registration card and on any election mailings. All polling places are wheelchair-accessible. Curbside voting is available upon request.

Precinct polling locations

  • Precinct 1: Town Hall, Memorial Hall (1 Cobbett Square)
  • Precinct 2: Public Library Community Room (22 Cobbett Square)
  • Precinct 3: Harbor District Fire Station (47 Wharf Street)
  • Precinct 4: Cobbett River Elementary School (102 Old Hill Road)

Voters in line at 8:00 p.m. will be permitted to vote. Acceptable identification is not required to vote in Massachusetts but may be requested in certain cases.

Pothole & Street Defect Reports

Office
Department of Public Works
Phone
(774) 555-0105
Response goal
72 hours for hazardous defects
Fee
None (residents)

Report potholes, deteriorated pavement, missing or damaged signs, broken curbing, blocked storm drains, and other street-related defects. Reports may be submitted online, by phone, or through the town’s SeeClickFix integration. State-numbered routes (Route 6, Route 28A) should be reported to MassDOT.

What to include

  • Street address or nearest intersection
  • Description of the defect and its size
  • Photograph if possible
  • Your contact information (optional but helpful)

For defects posing immediate safety hazards (large potholes, missing manhole covers, downed signs), please call (774) 555-0105 directly. After business hours, dial 911 for hazards in the travel lane.

Property Tax Payments

Office
Tax Collector — Town Hall, Room 103
Phone
(774) 555-0103
Schedule
Quarterly: Aug 1, Nov 1, Feb 1, May 1
FY27 rate
$11.42 residential / $22.18 commercial

Real estate and personal property taxes are billed quarterly. Bills are mailed approximately 30 days before each due date. Payments not received by 4:30 p.m. on the due date are subject to interest at the statutory rate of 14% per annum.

Payment methods

  • Online: ACH (free), credit card (2.95% fee)
  • By mail: Tax Collector, P.O. Box 47, Millbrook MA 02XXX
  • In person: counter or 24-hour drop box outside Town Hall
  • Auto-pay: enroll to have payments drafted on each due date

Exemptions available

The Assessor administers several statutory exemptions: elderly (Clause 41C), veterans (Clauses 22, 22A–F), surviving spouse (Clause 17D), and blind (Clause 37A). Applications are due April 1.

Services beginning with R

Public Records Requests

Office
Records Access Officer — Town Manager’s Office
Phone
(774) 555-0101
Email
rao@millbrook-ma.gov
Response
10 business days (statutory)

Massachusetts Public Records Law guarantees the public’s right of access to government records. Requests do not need to be in writing, do not need to state a purpose, and may be made by anyone. Routine records (meeting minutes, agendas, contracts) are typically released the same day at no charge.

How to request

  1. Describe the record(s) with reasonable specificity.
  2. Submit by email, mail, or in person to the RAO.
  3. The RAO will respond within 10 business days.
  4. If responsive records exist, you will receive them or a fee estimate.

Fees

  • Black-and-white copies: $0.05 per page
  • Color copies: $0.15 per page
  • Staff time (after first four hours): $25/hour
  • Electronic records: typically free

Some records are exempt from disclosure (personnel files, certain investigative records, attorney-client communications). The RAO will identify any exemptions claimed and the legal basis.

Submit a records request Records access guide Common record types & fees

Shellfish Permits (Recreational)

Office
Harbormaster — 47 Wharf Street
Phone
(774) 555-0114
Season
Year-round (subject to closures)
Fee
Resident $30 / Senior $15 / Non-resident $85

Recreational shellfishing for soft-shell clams, quahogs, and oysters is permitted in designated areas of Millbrook Bay with a valid annual permit. Permits are issued by the Harbormaster’s office. Permit-holders must observe daily limits, gear restrictions, and posted closures.

Daily limits

  • Soft-shell clams: 10 quarts per day
  • Quahogs: 1 peck per day (cherrystone or larger)
  • Oysters: 1/2 bushel per day (minimum 3-inch shell)

Closures

Beds are closed seasonally for spawning, after heavy rainfall (24–72 hours), and following bacterial sampling above safe thresholds. Always check current status before harvesting. Violations are subject to fines starting at $100.

Current bed status Permit application Shellfish regulations

Restaurants and cafes may apply to operate seasonal outdoor seating on public sidewalks. Permits require maintenance of a minimum five-foot clear path of travel, ADA-accessible routes, and removable barriers separating dining areas from pedestrian traffic.

Smoke & CO Alarm Inspections (Resale)

Office
Fire Department — 4 Cobbett Square
Phone
(774) 555-0111
Lead time
Schedule 2–3 weeks before closing
Fees
1 unit: $50; 2 units: $100; 3+ units: $150

Massachusetts law requires inspection of smoke and carbon monoxide alarms before the sale of any residential property. Inspections verify that alarms are properly installed, of the correct type, and in working condition. The Fire Department issues a Certificate of Compliance valid for 60 days.

Before your inspection

  • Install alarms on every level and in every bedroom.
  • Ensure photoelectric smoke alarms within 20 ft. of cooking appliances.
  • Install CO alarms within 10 ft. of each bedroom.
  • Test every alarm and replace any older than 10 years.
Schedule inspection Alarm requirements guide

Snow Removal & Sidewalk Bylaws

Office
Department of Public Works
Phone
(774) 555-0105
Deadline
12 hours after storm ends
Fine
$50 first offense, $100 thereafter

Town bylaw requires property owners to clear snow and ice from sidewalks abutting their property within 12 hours of the end of a storm (or by noon the following day, whichever is later). The DPW clears town-maintained sidewalks in the downtown business district.

Parking ban

When the Police Chief declares a winter parking ban (typically when 2+ inches of snow is forecast), parking is prohibited on all town streets from 9:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m. Vehicles will be towed at the owner’s expense.

Senior & disabled assistance

Residents 70+ or with documented disabilities may request volunteer assistance with snow removal through the Council on Aging’s Shovel Brigade program. Sign-ups open November 1.

Report streetlights that are out, flickering, or staying on during daylight hours. Each town-owned streetlight bears a small numbered tag (6 digits) approximately eight feet above the ground; providing this number speeds repair. Lights owned by the utility company are tagged with the company logo.

Trash & Recycling Pickup

Office
Department of Public Works
Phone
(774) 555-0105
Schedule
Weekly trash, bi-weekly recycling
Fee
Included in property taxes

Curbside collection is provided to all single- and two-family homes in Millbrook. Place barrels at the curb by 6:30 a.m. on your collection day. Trash is collected weekly; recycling is collected on alternating weeks. Holidays may delay collection by one day.

Collection days by zone

  • Zone A (downtown, Cobbett Square): Monday
  • Zone B (eastern hill, Old Hill Road): Tuesday
  • Zone C (Harbor District, Wharf St area): Wednesday
  • Zone D (north farms, Forest Road): Thursday
  • Zone E (south, Mill Road, industrial): Friday

Accepted recycling

  • Paper, cardboard (flattened), magazines, junk mail
  • Glass bottles & jars (rinsed)
  • Aluminum and steel cans
  • Plastic containers #1, #2, #5 (rinsed)

Plastic bags, styrofoam, and food-soiled paper are not accepted in curbside recycling. Bring plastic bags to grocery store drop-offs and bring styrofoam to the quarterly recycling drop-off events.

The Tree Warden has authority over all trees within town rights-of-way and on town property. Removal of any public tree requires a posted public hearing under M.G.L. c. 87. Report dead or dangerous public trees, request a planting (sponsored or memorial), or apply to remove a public tree.

Vital Records (Birth, Marriage, Death)

Town Clerk — Town Hall, Room 102
Phone
(774) 555-0102
Records held
1738 – present

The Town Clerk maintains vital records for all births, marriages, and deaths recorded in Millbrook. Certified copies are typically required for school enrollment, passport application, insurance claims, estate matters, and pension benefits. Records older than 90 years are unrestricted; recent records require identification.

How to request

  1. In person: walk-in service available during office hours.
  2. By mail: complete the Vital Records Request Form with $10 per copy plus a self-addressed stamped envelope.
  3. Online: with credit card and government-issued ID upload.

Required information

Voter Registration

Office
Town Clerk — Town Hall, Room 102
Phone
(774) 555-0102
Cutoff
10 days before election
Fee
None

You may register to vote if you are a United States citizen, a Massachusetts resident, and at least 16 years old (you may register at 16 but cannot vote until you turn 18). Registration may be completed online, in person, or by mail. Same-day registration is also available on election days.

How to register

  • Online: at the Massachusetts Online Voter Registration portal with a valid driver’s license or state ID.
  • In person: at the Town Clerk, Public Library, RMV, or any state agency.
  • By mail: complete a registration form and mail to the Town Clerk.
  • Same-day: register and vote at your polling place on Election Day with proof of residency.

You will receive a confirmation by mail within two weeks. If you do not, contact the Town Clerk. To check your registration status, search the state’s voter information lookup.

Water & Sewer Bills

Office
Water Department — 12 Cobbett Square
Phone
(774) 555-0150
Schedule
Quarterly billing
Rates
$5.25 per 100 cu. ft. (tier 1)

Millbrook bills water and sewer charges quarterly based on metered consumption. Bills are mailed about 30 days before due dates. Tiered rates encourage conservation: tier 1 (first 1,500 cu. ft.) is the lowest; tier 3 (above 4,500 cu. ft.) is highest. Sewer is billed at 110% of metered water use.

Payment methods

  • Online with bill number (ACH free; card 2.95% fee)
  • Auto-pay enrollment (drafts on due date)
  • Mail: Water Dept., P.O. Box 51, Millbrook, MA 02XXX
  • In person or after-hours drop box at 12 Cobbett Square

Assistance programs

  • Senior discount (age 65+, income limits): 15% reduction
  • Income-eligible hardship credit (apply through COA)
  • Leak adjustment (one-time, with plumber’s repair receipt)

Yard Sale Permits

Office
Town Clerk — Town Hall, Room 102
Phone
(774) 555-0102
Limit
3 sales per address per calendar year
Fee
$5 per sale

Residents holding yard sales, garage sales, or estate sales must obtain a permit from the Town Clerk. Permits are available the same day. Sales are limited to three per address per calendar year and to weekends only (Friday 4:00 p.m. through Sunday 8:00 p.m.).

Sign placement

  • Signs may be placed on private property with the owner’s consent.
  • Signs are prohibited on town poles, signposts, and within rights-of-way.
  • All signs must be removed within 24 hours of the sale.

Annual community-wide yard sale day is held the first Saturday in May. Participating residents who register pay a single $5 fee that covers the day.
